# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

Parent: [F\_255](F_255_make_diagrams_editable.md).

## Goal

Implement direct selection in the Select tool.

## Current state

* `DiagramEditSessionService` owns the active persistent tool, which defaults to `select`, and exposes a synchronous snapshot for event handlers.
* `DiagramSelectionService` already owns node, edge, and group selection as stable `{ objectKind, objectId }` identities. It supports replacement and clearing plus identity-scoped subscriptions.
* Current renders through `DiagramRenderer`. Node and edge activation opens the existing child-action or saved-diagram menu; groups are non-interactive and nodes with `drilldown: false` cannot activate that menu.
* New renders through `DiagramZoomViewport` and service-bound editable leaves. Its comparison layouts do not connect node or edge activation to selection, groups have `pointerEvents: 'none'`, and no leaf renders its selected state. Clicking New background therefore does not clear selection.

## Implementation details

* Keep direct selection inside New. Pass `DiagramSelectionService` as an injectable service dependency through `DiagramZoomViewport`, `EditableDiagram`, collection hosts, and selectable leaves; do not route New activation through `DiagramViewService` or its menu payload.
* Add a selection hook backed by `useSyncExternalStore`. Each selectable leaf subscribes with `subscribeSelected` and reads `getSelectedSnapshot` for its own stable identity only.
* On pointer activation, read `getActiveToolSnapshot()`. When the active tool is exactly `select`, call `replace` with the activated node, edge, or group identity. Do not add Ctrl-click toggle behavior; F_292 owns additive selection.
* Make New groups pointer- and keyboard-operable. Make every New node selectable, including `drilldown: false` nodes; that field controls Current drill-down only. Enter and Space perform the same replacement as a pointer click and prevent their browser default.
* Handle bubbling clicks at the New drawing surface. If the event has no selectable node, edge, or group ancestor and Select is active, call `clear`. This includes blank areas covered by the connections SVG, while an object click must not be cleared after its leaf handler runs.
* Give shared node, edge, and group primitives explicit caller-owned interaction and selected presentation inputs. Verified call sites diverge intentionally: `Diagram` keeps Current node and edge drill-down behavior plus non-interactive groups; editable leaves use selection behavior for all three object kinds. No other call sites require another mode.
* Mark selected objects with accessible selected state and theme-backed treatment: `primary.main` for outline or edge stroke and `custom.primaryBg` for any halo or tint. Keep keyboard focus visible. Do not add raw colors or replace role-based node styling.
* Keep selection outside diagram model, geometry, and change tracking. Selection changes must not publish edit-session field or collection events.
* Add user-interaction tests for pointer activation, Enter and Space, empty-surface clearing, inactive-tool guards, `drilldown: false` nodes, all three object kinds, Current regressions, and leaf render isolation.

## Acceptance criteria

* While Select is active, plain-clicking a New node, edge, or group replaces the complete selection with that object's stable kind and ID. A New node remains selectable when `drilldown` is `false`.
* While Select is active, clicking New drawing-surface space with no selectable object under the pointer clears selection. Object activation is not cleared by the same bubbling event.
* Pointer or keyboard activation while another persistent tool is active does not change selection or open a drill-down menu.
* Enter and Space select the focused New node, edge, or group without opening the Current child-action menu.
* Every selected New object exposes accessible selected state and a visible treatment sourced from `primary.main` and, where a halo or tint is used, `custom.primaryBg`. Keyboard focus remains visible in both light and dark themes.
* Current remains read-only: node and edge activation retains its child-action and saved-diagram menu behavior, `drilldown: false` nodes remain non-interactive, and groups remain non-interactive.
* Direct selection changes no diagram object, geometry, edit change, viewport state, or comparison layout state.
* Replacing selection rerenders only leaves whose selected boolean changed. Clearing rerenders only previously selected leaves; diagram roots, collection hosts, and unrelated leaves do not rerender.

## State and rendering rule

A click invokes the selection service only. The clicked and previously selected leaves observe their own selected booleans; the diagram root, object collections, and unrelated objects do not subscribe to selection as a complete list and do not rerender.

Parent: [F\_255](F_255_make_diagrams_editable.md).

## Goal

Add a selection service for nodes, edges, and groups in the active edit session.

## Scope

Store selections as object kind plus stable object ID. Use `EventTarget`, granular events, and stable snapshots. Remove missing identities after diagram mutations and clear on session reset.

## Acceptance criteria

* Selection never uses array index, label, DOM element, or file path as identity.
* The service supports replace, add, remove, toggle, clear, and membership queries.
* Deleting an object removes it from selection before publication.
* Multiple subscribers receive scoped updates without revision counters.

## State and rendering rule

Selection is stored by stable identity and updated without replacing a selected diagram object. Each selectable leaf subscribes to its own selected boolean. A selection-membership snapshot changes only when membership changes; diagram roots, object collections, unrelated leaves, and model data do not rerender or change.

## Dependencies

[F\_275](F_275_add_diagram_edit_session_service.md).

## Goal

Allow Ctrl-click to add or remove individual objects from selection.

## Acceptance criteria

* Ctrl-clicking an unselected node, edge, or group adds it.
* Ctrl-clicking a selected object removes only that object.
* Plain click still replaces selection.
* The behavior works with mixed object kinds and does not trigger moving, resizing, or drill-down.
* Tests use actual user interaction rather than service internals.

## State and rendering rule

Ctrl-click changes one identity's selected membership in place and dispatches events only for that identity plus the selection-membership view used by selection-specific controls. It does not publish diagram data or rebuild selected objects.

---

When an action runs an agent, we track the number of lines that were changed and removed. This works ok.

However, when codex runs tasks in parallel, we only seem to show the nr of lines that the root agent changed, not what the sub agents did.

We should show the total lines changed below the action popup's conversation log, across all agents that ran in parallel.

## Current state

The usage footer already sums every completed `fileChange` entry in the canonical conversation. Codex reports spawned agents through `subAgentActivity` items, but the desktop adapter does not support that item type or hydrate the referenced child thread. The child agent's file changes therefore never reach the conversation, so the footer can only count root-agent changes.

## Implementation details

- Handle Codex `subAgentActivity` items and register their `agentThreadId` as soon as the activity starts.
- Accept live notifications from registered child threads and tag their events with the owning sub-agent activity.
- When a child activity completes, read the child thread's turns and normalize any completed `fileChange` items that were not received live. Recursively discover nested sub-agent activities.
- Namespace provider item identities by thread ID and deduplicate live and hydrated events.
- Wait for the finite set of pending child-thread reads before publishing the root conversation as complete. Log a child-thread read failure and continue safely without inventing counts.
- Store child file changes through the existing canonical conversation event path. The existing usage footer aggregation remains unchanged.
- Add focused tests in the Codex adapter and usage aggregation suites for parallel agents, nested agents, live/history deduplication, and child-thread read failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The conversation usage footer includes insertions and deletions reported by the root agent and every spawned Codex sub-agent.
- [ ] Parallel and nested sub-agent file changes are included exactly once.
- [ ] Live child-thread events and hydrated thread history cannot double-count the same file change.
- [ ] The root conversation does not complete before pending child-thread file-change reads finish.
- [ ] A failed child-thread read is logged, does not fail the action, and does not fabricate line counts.
- [ ] Existing root-only and non-Codex file-change reporting remains unchanged.
- [ ] Focused desktop and app tests pass.

id: F_422

title: check if possible to switch agent accounts
status: ready for implementation
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__733d678c-49a7-4409-9fa2-5fb384821513.json
policy:
branch: f_422_check_if_possible_to_switch_agent_accounts
---

Allow separate Codex and Claude accounts to be configured, selected as defaults, assigned to actions and runs, and remembered by provider sessions in a conversation.

## Current state

* MDÂ² has one effective account per CLI. `AgentRunnerService`, model discovery, and account-usage polling copy the desktop process environment, so every Codex process uses the same Codex login and every Claude process uses the same Claude login.
* The existing global logins are the initial primary accounts:
  * Codex uses its normal `CODEX_HOME` (default `%USERPROFILE%\.codex`). File-based authentication is stored in `auth.json`; Codex can alternatively use the operating-system credential store.
  * Claude uses its normal `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (default `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`). On Windows, authentication is stored in `.credentials.json` in that directory.
* Codex supports a separate state directory through `CODEX_HOME`. Claude supports the same pattern through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Both variables select a complete CLI configuration directory, including credentials and other CLI state.
* Desktop agent selection stores `activeAgent`, one permission mode, and model, reasoning, and speed settings in `settingsByAgent`. There is no account collection or default account setting.
* Action definitions and run requests can override agent, model, reasoning, speed, and permission mode. Their schemas, editors, validation, history, and card-level remembered settings have no account field.
* A conversation stores provider sessions by `agent` only. Continuation and compaction therefore assume that every session for an agent belongs to the single global login.
* Model catalogs and Claude/Codex rate-limit snapshots are also keyed only by agent. Account-reset schedules and `usage_metrics.csv` cannot distinguish two accounts of the same provider.
* The config dialog has a specialized agent-profile editor, but there is no account-management service, directory picker, login bridge, or account editor.

## Implementation details

### Account model and desktop configuration

* Add a validated `desktop.agentAccounts` configuration value. Store accounts per supported built-in agent (`codex` and `claude`). Do not infer account support for custom agent profiles because MDÂ² does not know which configuration-directory variable they use.
* An account record contains:
  * `id`: stable identity used by selections, actions, runs, schedules, metrics, and conversations. Generate a UUID for extra accounts. Use stable reserved IDs for the two primary accounts.
  * `name`: editable display name. For an extra account, initialize it from the selected configuration folder name.
  * `kind`: `primary` or `directory`.
  * `configDirectory`: absolute directory path for a `directory` account only. The path is a persistence location and must never be used as account identity.
* Always resolve one primary account as the first account for Codex and one for Claude. A primary account has no configured directory: processes run with the normal inherited CLI environment and continue using the login already configured outside MDÂ². It can be renamed but cannot have its directory changed or be removed.
* Migrate existing desktop configuration by adding the two primary records and assigning the appropriate primary account to every existing `settingsByAgent` entry. This reflects historical behavior: all existing runs used the global CLI login.
* Add `accountId` to `AgentSettings` and `FlatAgentSelection`. The value in `settingsByAgent[agent]` is that agent's default account. Add `selectAccount`, validation that the account belongs to the selected agent, and resolution that returns the selected account with the existing profile/model settings.
* Reject duplicate account IDs a
[7320 characters omitted]
ite the new header for new files. Do not combine percentage deltas from different accounts.
* Add `accountId` to account-reset schedule triggers, tracker keys, snapshots, labels, persistence, and validation. Existing schedules migrate to the primary account for their agent.
* Record run token usage with the run's account ID. Record rate-limit usage with the account whose environment produced the snapshot.

### Failure handling and compatibility

* A renamed account remains valid because references use `accountId`. A moved, missing, or unreadable extra directory makes only that account unavailable and offers directory reselection or login retry.
* Changing the default account affects only new provider sessions and runs without an explicit account. Existing provider sessions continue with their stored account.
* Logging out or expiring credentials does not trigger fallback to another account. Show a login-required state and keep unrelated accounts usable.
* Existing desktop config, action files, card action settings, conversations, activity records, schedules, and usage metrics require explicit migrations to the primary account where described above.

### Tests

* Shared/config tests: primary-account migration, account validation, stable IDs across rename, unique directories, `selectAccount`, default resolution, and explicit missing-account errors.
* Account service tests: primary environment, Codex/Claude directory environments, folder validation, login command construction, cancellation/failure, status reporting, and confirmation that credential content is never returned over the bridge.
* UI tests: config account creation/rename/retry, default account selection, action account selection, run-menu selection, and unavailable references.
* Action tests: parser/writer support, run-input allowlist, resolution precedence, activity/history persistence, scheduled actions, and remote-control payloads.
* Conversation tests: provider-session uniqueness by agent and account, same-account resume, first switch sending the full transcript, retry, compact using the stored account, and legacy sessions migrating to primary.
* Runtime tests: model catalogs and rate-limit snapshots remain isolated per account; polls use the correct environment and stop cleanly.
* Metrics/schedule tests: account IDs separate baselines and reset trackers, while legacy data resolves to primary.
* Run the directly affected app and desktop tests, then `npm run lint` in both subprojects. Do not run the full test suites unless requested.

## Acceptance criteria

* Every installed Codex and Claude CLI has a primary account that uses its existing global login without moving or copying credentials.
* A user can add an extra account by selecting a configuration folder, completing the provider's login flow, and optionally changing the name derived from that folder.
* MDÂ² never asks for or transports provider usernames, passwords, or credential-file contents.
* The user can select a default account for each agent and can override it in an action definition and in the run menu.
* Runs, model discovery, usage polling, retries, and diagnostics use the selected account's configuration directory.
* A conversation remembers account identity per provider session. Continuing with the same agent and account resumes it; selecting another account starts a separate provider session and sends the full conversation context once.
* Changing defaults or account names does not change the account used by an existing provider session. Compact and resume never cross account boundaries.
* Rate limits, usage metrics, and account-reset schedules remain separate for accounts of the same provider.
* Existing configuration, actions, conversations, activity, schedules, and metrics continue under the primary account after migration.
* Missing folders, expired credentials, cancelled login, and unavailable referenced accounts produce clear errors without falling back to another account or preventing other accounts from running.
* Focused tests and lint pass in `app` and `desktop`.

---

id: F_446
internalId: 1a8109e1-2ead-482d-b6d0-c34fd94c0270
title: diagrams control key
status: ready for implementation
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__1a8109e1-2ead-482d-b6d0-c34fd94c0270.json
policy:
---

When user is working with the select tool he can click on items which selects them or he can draw a box which selects the items in the box. this works ok.

However, the system does not respond to the ctrl key. when this is pressed and the user clicks on another item or draws another selection box, then the newly selected items should be added to the already selected items and not replace them.

## Current state

* In the New diagram, Ctrl-click already toggles one node, edge, or group through `DiagramSelectionService.toggle`; plain click replaces selection.
* Rectangle selection starts on empty surface while Select is active. `EditableDiagramSurface` forwards only pointer coordinates, so `DiagramSelectionService.completeRectangleSelection` always replaces selection with intersecting objects. A zero-distance gesture clears selection.
* Selection service stores stable object kind and ID pairs, calculates intersecting nodes, edges, and groups, and publishes identity-scoped events. Selection changes do not modify diagram data or edit history.

## Implementation details

* In `EditableDiagramSurface`, capture `event.ctrlKey` when valid rectangle selection starts. Keep modifier state for that pointer gesture, then clear it after completion, cancellation, lost pointer capture, or tool change.
* Extend `DiagramSelectionService.completeRectangleSelection` with an additive flag. When additive, replace selection with union of current identities and rectangle intersections; existing identities remain selected and duplicates are removed by existing `replace` behavior. When not additive, keep current replacement behavior.
* Treat Ctrl plus a zero-distance or non-intersecting rectangle as adding no objects, so existing selection remains. Keep plain zero-distance and non-intersecting rectangle behavior unchanged: selection becomes empty.
* Keep existing node, edge, and group Ctrl-click handlers unchanged: Ctrl-click adds an unselected object and removes a selected object; plain click replaces selection.
* `EditableDiagramSurface` is only production caller of rectangle completion and receives new behavior. Existing service tests that omit additive flag retain replacement behavior.
* Add focused service and user-interaction tests for additive rectangle selection, mixed object kinds, duplicate intersections, empty rectangles, modifier capture, cancellation, inactive tools, and unchanged plain selection.

## Acceptance criteria

* While Select is active, Ctrl-clicking an unselected New diagram node, edge, or group adds it without removing other selected objects; Ctrl-clicking a selected object removes only that object.
* When Ctrl is held as rectangle drawing starts, completing rectangle adds every intersecting node, edge, and group to existing selection without duplicates or removals.
* A Ctrl-modified zero-distance or non-intersecting rectangle leaves existing selection unchanged.
* Without Ctrl, item clicks and completed rectangles continue replacing selection; a plain zero-distance or non-intersecting rectangle clears selection.
* Releasing or cancelling pointer gesture, losing pointer capture, or leaving Select clears captured modifier state. Another tool cannot start or complete rectangle selection.
* Additive selection changes only selection membership. Diagram data, geometry, edit history, viewport state, and unrelated selected-state subscribers remain unchanged.
